messages.content: The Raleigh host finally answered. Saturday should be done by 3, they can store demo equipment until Sunday, and I can preview the room Thursday evening. Can we finish the flight and hotel decision now?

Yes. With those answers, the practical plan is clear: use the suite hotel instead of the clinic-adjacent hotel, fly in on the Thursday evening nonstop if the fare is tolerable, and keep a Sunday afternoon return. The adjacent hotel still cannot confirm a refrigerator, so it is the shortest commute but the weakest room setup. The suite hotel confirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room; the only amenity caveat is that the hot tub is listed as seasonal and is not guaranteed.
Lay out the flight trade-off before I commit. I don’t want cheapest if it makes Friday miserable.

For Thursday March 6, the nonstop is the more practical choice: it gets you into RDU in the evening with enough margin to check in and still do the room preview. The cheaper connection saves about $120, but it lands after midnight if everything is on time, which is a bad setup before Friday teaching prep. For Sunday March 9, the afternoon nonstop is stronger than a Saturday evening departure because you are not rushing teardown, and the host has confirmed they can store gear until Sunday.
Okay, so the nonstop outbound is worth it. What hotel would you actually book?

I would book the suite hotel. Deciding reasons: confirmed mini-fridge and coffee maker, confirmed queen room, better recovery setup with indoor pool and fitness room, and still only about 15 minutes from the clinic. Caveats before booking: the hot tub may not be available, and it is not walkable to the clinic the way the adjacent hotel is. I would not book the adjacent hotel unless they put the refrigerator in writing.
Book the suite hotel, then. Queen room, and make sure the coffee maker and mini-fridge are in the confirmation notes.

I have the queen suite selected for Thursday March 6 through Sunday March 9. The room listing confirms coffee maker and mini-fridge, and I added a note asking the hotel to keep that room type assigned. Cancellation is allowed until two days before arrival; after that, one night becomes nonrefundable. Hot tub remains the only unconfirmed recovery item.
That’s fine. For Sunday, give me the best return that still doesn’t burn the whole day.

Best fit is the Sunday afternoon nonstop RDU to Tampa: departs mid-afternoon, arrives late afternoon, and avoids a connection. There is a cheaper one-stop later in the day, but it gets you home after 8 p.m. and adds delay risk for not much savings. Since you are released Saturday by 3 and the gear can stay onsite, there is no schedule reason to force a Saturday evening flight.
Book the Sunday afternoon nonstop. Window seat if the seat map lets you. Same for the Thursday flight.

Seat map is open on both legs. I can put you in 18F on the Thursday evening nonstop to RDU and 14A on the Sunday afternoon nonstop back to Tampa. Both are window seats. They are standard economy seats, not exit row.
Those are fine. Finalize it and send me the clean version.

Booked. Raleigh plan is now: Thursday March 6 evening nonstop TPA-RDU, seat 18F window; suite hotel Thursday through Sunday with queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room confirmed; hot tub seasonal/not guaranteed; Thursday evening room preview with the host; Saturday teaching expected to finish by 3 p.m.; demo equipment can stay onsite until Sunday; Sunday March 9 afternoon nonstop RDU-TPA, seat 14A window. Main caveats: the hotel hot tub is not guaranteed, and you should avoid the clinic-adjacent hotel unless they later confirm the refrigerator in writing.

messages.content: Raleigh update: enrollment went up, and Friday check-in is now at a staff-only clinic entrance on the back side of the building. I’ll have one extra demo bag. Do I need a rental car after all?

I do not think a compact rental is worth it unless you need to make supply runs. The host can store gear through Sunday, so this is mainly a Friday morning drop-off problem. Better plan: reserve an XL rideshare or local car-service SUV, pin the back entrance, and add a driver note about the rolling demo bag plus duffel.
Is an early Friday XL reliable enough there? I don’t want to be circling the wrong entrance at 7 a.m.

For reliability, I would use a scheduled local car-service SUV if the price is reasonable, with XL rideshare as backup. It costs more than a basic ride, but still avoids rental pickup, parking, and keeping a car you barely use. The key is giving the driver the exact entrance language and the host contact number.
Let’s skip the rental. Set up the SUV option if they can handle one large roller and one duffel.

I can set it for Friday morning hotel pickup at 6:45, destination note: “staff-only clinic entrance on back side of building, not main lobby.” Vehicle request: SUV, one passenger, one large rolling demo bag, one duffel. I will also keep a rideshare XL backup window open in case the driver cancels.
Good. Does the Thursday arrival still work with the room preview?

Yes. Your Thursday nonstop still lands early enough for hotel check-in and the evening room preview, assuming no major delay. I kept the late-arrival note on the hotel anyway, so the room is protected if the flight slips.
Confirm the hotel details one more time. Especially the fridge.

Confirmed with the hotel: queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room are attached to the reservation. Hot tub is still uncertain because they list it as seasonal. Friday transport is now the scheduled SUV to the back clinic entrance with the extra demo bag noted, and the Sunday afternoon return still fits because the host does not need the equipment out Saturday night. Main caveat left: if the SUV driver misses the entrance, call the host before unloading rather than dragging the bags through the main lobby.
